hubs.name: RAG
senses: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): a framework/pipeline that combines an external document retrieval mechanism with a generative language model to ground outputs.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), including its pipelines, components, evaluation, and applications in knowledge-grounded language generation.

hubs.name: NDCG@10
senses: Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at rank 10 (NDCG@10), a widely used ranking and retrieval evaluation metric.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same standard information retrieval evaluation metric, Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at cutoff rank 10 (NDCG@10).

hubs.name: LLM
senses: Large Language Model (LLM): a class of foundation models trained on extensive text datasets for natural language understanding, generation, and reasoning across various downstream tasks.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe Large Language Models (LLMs), their capabilities, variants, and applications across tasks such as recommendation, evaluation, user simulation, and retrieval.

hubs.name: Semantic ID
senses: A discrete item identifier or tokenization representation constructed from semantic content, commonly used in generative retrieval and recommendation systems.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe Semantic IDs (or SIDs) as discrete semantic representations/identifiers assigned to items for generative sequential recommendation and retrieval.

hubs.name: BM25
senses: A widely used lexical ranking and retrieval algorithm (Okapi BM25) based on probabilistic information retrieval
hubs.reason: All fragments refer to the standard BM25 lexical ranking and retrieval algorithm used as a baseline, first-stage retriever, or sparse retrieval component.

hubs.name: BEIR
senses: A widely-used heterogeneous benchmark and dataset collection for evaluating zero-shot information retrieval models across various domains and tasks.
hubs.reason: All fragments uniformly refer to the BEIR benchmark (Benchmarking Information Retrieval), a standard evaluation benchmark in IR containing diverse datasets such as NQ and ArguAna.

hubs.name: NDCG
senses: Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG), a standard evaluation metric measuring the quality of ranking in information retrieval and recommender systems.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same evaluation metric, Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG / nDCG), used across various ranking, retrieval, and recommendation benchmarks.

hubs.name: Generative Recommendation
senses: A recommender system paradigm that frames recommendation as an autoregressive generation task over item tokens or identifiers.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same recommendation paradigm where recommendation is reformulated as sequence/autoregressive generation over discrete item tokens or representations.

hubs.name: MuSeR
senses: MuSeR: a multi-interest, long-sequence industrial recommendation system model developed and deployed in Baidu App
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same industrial recommender system model (MuSeR), its architecture (hierarchical temporal compression, multi-interest extraction, asynchronous caching), deployment details (Baidu App, Consul), and evaluation metrics.

hubs.name: Recall@10
senses: Recall@10 (or R@10), an information retrieval and recommendation evaluation metric measuring the proportion of relevant items retrieved in the top 10 positions.
hubs.reason: All fragments refer to the standard information retrieval and recommendation metric Recall@10 (also abbreviated as R@10).

hubs.name: Open Tabular Insight Extraction
senses: A research framework and task focused on discovering and deriving analytical insights and knowledge from large-scale tabular corpora.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the Open Tabular Insight Extraction (OpenTI) framework and task, detailing its definitions, associated insight types, system requirements, evaluation metrics, and capabilities.

hubs.name: AUC
senses: Area Under the Curve (AUC), a standard machine learning evaluation metric measuring the discriminatory or ranking capability of classification models
hubs.reason: All fragments consistently refer to the AUC evaluation metric (Area Under the ROC Curve or Area Under Curve) applied across various recommendation, classification, and ranking tasks.

hubs.name: HotpotQA
senses: HotpotQA is a multi-hop question answering and information retrieval benchmark dataset based on Wikipedia.
hubs.reason: All fragments consistently refer to the same well-known multi-hop question answering benchmark dataset HotpotQA.

hubs.name: LLM-as-a-Judge
senses: A paradigm or framework where a large language model is employed to evaluate, score, or select candidate text, outputs, or relevance judgments.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same methodological paradigm of using an LLM to evaluate or judge candidate outputs, reformulations, or quality metrics across various downstream tasks.

hubs.name: FINALLY
senses: A tool and framework designed to select, inspect, and construct configurable dataset sets for offline recommender-systems evaluations using diversity measures (such as EffCov) and APS visualizations.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same tool, FINALLY, which assists in dataset selection, metadata filtering, and visualization for recommender-system evaluations.

hubs.name: Reddit Answers
senses: Reddit Answers is an AI-powered generative search and answer synthesis system developed by or for Reddit that retrieves and synthesizes community comments to answer user queries.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the exact same concept: Reddit Answers, an AI-driven question answering and comment synthesis system/feature evaluated for its retrieval, selection biases, and synthesis behavior.

hubs.name: UNIQUE
senses: A unified retrieval and ranking recommendation framework using semantic code prediction and early fusion for mobile feed recommendations
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same recommendation framework (UNIQUE), detailing its architecture (Unified Early-Fusion Encoder, target-aware ranking path), training objectives (feedback-aware codebook learning loss, generative cross-entropy), and evaluation results (CTR-AUC, P99 latency, A/B testing).

hubs.name: BRIGHT
senses: A benchmark for reasoning-intensive information retrieval containing diverse reasoning-focused subsets such as BRIGHT-Code and TheoremQA.
hubs.reason: All fragments refer to the BRIGHT retrieval benchmark, which is used to evaluate retrieval, ranking, and RAG systems across various reasoning-intensive subsets.

hubs.name: Amazon Beauty
senses: A standard benchmark dataset of user reviews and interactions in the beauty category on Amazon, widely used in recommender systems research.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe evaluations of various recommendation models and algorithms on the Amazon Beauty dataset.

hubs.name: Q2D-Web
senses: A benchmark dataset designed to evaluate first-stage retrievers in agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines under realistic, production-scale web corpus conditions.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same retrieval benchmark dataset, Q2D-Web, detailing its corpus construction, evaluation metrics, and role in testing retrievers for agentic RAG systems.

hubs.name: Transformer
senses: A deep learning architecture based on self-attention mechanisms, widely used as an encoder, decoder, or backbone in recommendation, sequence modeling, and language tasks.
hubs.reason: All fragments refer to the standard Transformer neural network architecture (Vaswani et al.) and its standard components/applications across sequential recommendation, generative modeling, and audio/tabular processing.

hubs.name: Dense Retrieval
senses: An information retrieval paradigm where queries and documents are mapped into continuous dense vector representations to enable search via vector similarity and nearest-neighbor matching.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same well-known information retrieval paradigm of dense retrieval (vector-based retrieval using neural embeddings).

hubs.name: APCL
senses: A contrastive learning-based recommendation model for personalized fashion matching and complementary recommendation
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same model, APCL, which employs functional-view contrastive learning and indirect relational learning for personalized fashion and complementary item recommendation, evaluated on datasets like IQON3000.

hubs.name: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
senses: A rank aggregation algorithm in information retrieval that combines multiple ranked candidate lists into a single consolidated ranking based on reciprocal rank scores.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same standard information retrieval method, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), used to ensemble or merge ranking lists from different retrieval systems or models.

hubs.name: MuSiQue
senses: MuSiQue (Multi-hop Questions via Single-hop Question Composition) is a multi-hop question answering benchmark dataset used to evaluate retrieval and QA models.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same concept: MuSiQue, a standard multi-hop question answering dataset used as an evaluation benchmark for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and downstream QA models.

hubs.name: FedHUR
senses: A federated recommendation framework/model that learns and mines hierarchical utility-guided client relations to perform collaborative aggregation.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same federated recommendation model (FedHUR), including its modules, evaluation baselines/metrics, and communication compression techniques.

hubs.name: AURA
senses: An automated diagnostic and code-fix pipeline/framework deployed on streaming platforms to diagnose recommendation failure modes and generate/verify fixes.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe stages, evaluation methods, and deployment details of the same automated recommendation diagnosis and repair system (AURA).

hubs.name: MRR
senses: Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), an information retrieval and ranking evaluation metric measuring the reciprocal rank of the first relevant item, often evaluated at rank cutoff k.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same standard ranking metric, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), including its variations at rank cutoffs (MRR@k) and applications to evaluate retrievers, LLM recommendation prominence, or job matching.

hubs.name: Cassette
senses: A retrieval model/framework for legal case retrieval (LCR) that uses structural knowledge distillation from a teacher retriever to student encoders.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same legal case retrieval model named Cassette, highlighting its architecture (student candidate encoders, MLP for queries, teacher distillation) and evaluation metrics.

hubs.name: Query Performance Prediction
senses: A task and set of methods in information retrieval aimed at estimating or predicting the retrieval quality/effectiveness of a search query without ground-truth relevance judgments.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe Query Performance Prediction (QPP) in information retrieval, including its methods, metrics (e.g., AUROC, ECE, Spearman correlation), and applications.

hubs.name: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
senses: A 0.6-billion-parameter text embedding model from the Qwen family evaluated and fine-tuned for retrieval tasks and quantization.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same specific model, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (or Qwen3-Emb-0.6B), discussing its performance, fine-tuning, and quantization behavior across retrieval benchmarks.

hubs.name: TIGER
senses: A generative recommendation framework that uses semantic identifiers from RQ-VAE and an autoregressive Transformer backbone for sequential retrieval
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same generative recommendation model (TIGER), which generates discrete semantic identifiers for items using a quantized autoencoder and transformer backbone.

hubs.name: Generative Retrieval
senses: An information retrieval paradigm in which a model directly generates document or item identifiers (e.g., semantic IDs, URLs, or discrete codes) given a query, rather than relying on index-based dense/sparse matching or multi-stage filtering.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same information retrieval paradigm ('generative retrieval') where generative models directly output identifiers of relevant items or documents.

hubs.name: SASRec
senses: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation (SASRec), a widely used transformer-based sequential recommendation model.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe SASRec, a well-known self-attentive sequential recommendation baseline model, used for candidate drafting, evaluation, or as a backbone model across various recommender systems tasks.

hubs.name: TimelyRAG
senses: A retriever-agnostic, semantic-temporal hybrid reranking framework for retrieval-augmented generation designed for time-critical question answering.
hubs.reason: All fragments consistently describe TimelyRAG, a temporal reranking framework for retrieval-augmented generation that combines semantic similarity with temporal compatibility.

hubs.name: Constrained Hybrid Decoding
senses: A speculative retrieval-augmented generation decoding framework (CHyD) that alternates between free autoregressive generation and constrained verbatim extraction to guarantee faithful evidence retrieval.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same method, Constrained Hybrid Decoding (CHyD), an approach using speculative decoding architectures to guarantee verbatim evidence extraction in retrieval-augmented generation.

hubs.name: PDMR
senses: A generative retrieval model that adapts fine-grained token-level matching principles from ColBERT for identifier design, evaluated on retrieval benchmarks such as NQ320K and MS MARCO Document.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same generative retrieval method, detailing its identifier design inspired by ColBERT, training with DocT5Query, and evaluation benchmarks against dense and generative baselines.

hubs.name: LoRA
senses: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique for neural network architectures
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the use, configuration, or comparison of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapters for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of neural networks.

hubs.name: PCGNet
senses: A multi-objective graph learning model for personalized fashion matching that jointly models compatibility and personal preferences.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same PCGNet architecture and its evaluations on datasets like Polyvore-U-519 and IQON3000 for personalized fashion matching.

hubs.name: F1 Score
senses: A standard machine learning and natural language processing evaluation metric defined as the harmonic mean of precision and recall.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same well-known evaluation metric, F1 Score, detailing its definition, applications across various benchmarks (e.g., MuSiQue, LoCoMo), and usage in decision-making and performance evaluation.

hubs.name: SURF
senses: Subtractive Updates for Recommender Forgetting (SURF), a machine unlearning framework for recommender systems
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same method, SURF (Subtractive Updates for Recommender Forgetting), which is an unlearning framework designed for recommender systems to efficiently remove the influence of specified data.

hubs.name: Supervised Fine-Tuning
senses: A standard machine learning training phase where a pre-trained model is adapted using labeled input-output demonstration pairs.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), a well-established machine learning technique used for adapting pre-trained models to specific tasks or domains using labeled supervision.

hubs.name: G3RAG
senses: Geometric Gain Graph RAG (G3RAG), a document-only graph retrieval-augmented generation framework designed for multi-hop retrieval and reasoning using geometric gain scores and controlled transient diffusion
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same retrieval-augmented generation system, its components, evaluation metrics, and architectural mechanisms.

hubs.name: P3Rec
senses: A recommender system model that distills prior and posterior preference knowledge derived from LLM reasoning into a lightweight recommendation model.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same recommendation model (P3Rec), its architectural components (Interest Entropy Calibration, Prior-Posterior Preference Internalization), training objectives (preference absorption distillation loss), and experimental evaluations.

hubs.name: Recall
senses: A standard information retrieval and classification metric measuring the proportion of relevant items retrieved out of all relevant items.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the standard evaluation metric Recall (including variants such as Recall@K) used in information retrieval, recommendation, and classification.

hubs.name: Sequential Recommendation
senses: A recommendation paradigm and task setting that models chronologically ordered sequences of past user behavioral interactions to predict upcoming or subsequent interactions.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same well-known task in recommender systems, along with various models (GRU4Rec, BERT4Rec, CBiT, etc.) designed or evaluated for it.

hubs.name: VikingRAG
senses: A structure-aware retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework and hierarchical semantic data management system engineered for structured documents.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same retrieval-augmented generation system, detailing its architecture, components, evaluation metrics, and performance comparisons.

hubs.name: BGE-M3
senses: A multi-lingual, multi-functionality, and multi-granularity embedding model (BAAI General Embedding M3) used for text retrieval and evaluated under various tasks and quantization settings.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same embedding model, BGE-M3, focusing on its retrieval capabilities, benchmark evaluations, and sensitivity to post-training quantization.

hubs.name: EvoPilot
senses: An autonomous experiment control and research agent architecture featuring structured roles (Round Planner, Periodic Monitor, Failure Handler, Results Analyst) and memory systems for long-horizon asynchronous workflows.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same software/agent framework called EvoPilot, outlining its multi-role architecture, memory systems, failure handling, and workflow execution mechanisms.

hubs.name: Information Retrieval
senses: The academic field and computational task of finding and ranking relevant information, documents, or data from a collection to satisfy user queries and information needs.
hubs.reason: All fragments uniformly refer to the standard concept and task of Information Retrieval (IR) in computer science, including its metrics, systems, components, and integration with modern language models.
